subject.title: fix(ssh-verify): preserve active cooldown entries during prune

question: Should SSH verification cooldowns retain a strict 512-entry resource bound, or may active entries overflow that limit until their expiry?
rationale: The submitted implementation deliberately trades the existing hard cap for preserving every active cooldown, and source proof in the provided context does not establish which invariant is the intended product and availability contract.

options.title: Keep the hard cap
options.body: Retain bounded memory and revise the cooldown policy or keying so active entries do not cause premature re-probes without permitting unbounded growth.

options.title: Allow bounded-by-TTL overflow
options.body: Accept active-entry overflow explicitly, document its maximum lifetime and abuse controls, and add runtime and high-cardinality coverage.

options.title: Decline the behavior change
options.body: Keep current eviction semantics if the existing hard resource bound is the required gateway contract.

recommendation.title: Keep the hard cap
recommendation.body: Retain bounded memory and revise the cooldown policy or keying so active entries do not cause premature re-probes without permitting unbounded growth.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision concerns the gateway cooldown resource and retry contract in the affected module.
